title: Before the Bell
passages:
Sára woke before light, as she always did, and listened. Under the floorboards the iron wheel in the wall clicked over one tooth, the way it did every night, though no hand had ever turned it. On the kitchen table sat two things with paper tags. There had never been two.

Ákos was dressed, his letter in his pocket — the printing works at Vaskapu, answer due today. "Say something," he said. "Say I can go." "Not before the work," said Sára. "Say something about me." "Ask me after the Point," she said.

The first tag read: *For the woman in the Toll House. Open before the bell.* Every tag they had ever read said where a thing went. This one said open. The second thing was a doll, jointed, its face scraped smooth, tagged *For the house on the Point, before the bell, or it goes back.* Nobody had lived on the Point since the fire the year Ákos was born.

"You don't open them," Ákos said. "That's the rule. The Halászys opened theirs and forgot each other's names, and they've been polite about it ever since, and theirs was their own knocker back after forty years, so don't tell me nobody sends these." Sára tore the packet open. The tag had said to. Inside, a scrap of paper, and on it a name: VERA. She knew it the way you know a song you haven't heard in years. Ákos wrote VERA in his notebook over the first line, and did not read her what he crossed out. He put his letter back in his pocket, unopened. "Low tide's at noon." They took the lantern and the good boots and went out onto the causeway while the water still let them.
